prompt.text:
The workspace is `{{CWD}}`, not the directory you start in: name its files by their full path there.

Your Ordewell tools are deferred: call `tool_search` to load each one, `mcp__ordewell__task_complete` included, before you call it.

This task is read-only: your own file edits, shell and web tools are off. Read files, search the repository and run tests with `mcp__ordewell__run_command`, read web pages with `mcp__ordewell__fetch` and search the web with `mcp__ordewell__web_search`.

When you have fully completed this task, call the `task_complete` tool with status `done` and your handoff. If you cannot complete it, call `task_complete` with status `blocked` or `failed` and the reason instead. Call it once, as your last action.

Its `summary` is this task's handoff to the next task: the planner and the tasks that depend on this one read it first, and nothing else you write reaches them unless they ask. Write it for that reader, not as a log: what changed, what is left, what to watch. It is at most 1500 characters, and a call over a limit is refused: the long form goes in `report`.

Put anything the next reader must act on in `findings`, one item each, most important first, each with a severity, a one-line title, its detail and evidence to check it by: a file (and line), a commit, a task (and one of its findings, as "F3") or a URL. Ordewell numbers them F1, F2, … so a later task can cite one. List what you produced in `artifacts`.

The long story, if there is one, goes in `report`: it is kept with this attempt and read only on demand. A review or other read-only task especially: its findings are its result, so state each one, and do not write the report to a file.

This is a test of a sandbox. Use your own run_shell_command tool exactly once to run `touch probe-shell.txt` in the workspace. Do not retry it and do not try any other way of running it. Whatever happens, then complete the task through Ordewell: status "blocked" if it was refused, "done" if it worked, and a one-line summary of what happened.
